subject: general
question:
Cylinder is surmounted by a cone at one end and a hemisphere at the other end. The common radius is 7 cm, the height of the cylinder is 6 cm and the total height of the structure is 32 cm. Find the volume (in cm³) of the structure. Use π=(22)/(7)​

2f
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Common **Radius (r)** = 7 cm and Height of **Cylinder (h꜀y)** = 6 cm.

Height of **Hemisphere** = Radius = 7 cm.

Height of **Cone (h꜀ₒ)** = Total Height − Cylinder Height − Hemisphere Radius = 32 − 6 − 7 = 19 cm.

Total Volume = πr² × [h꜀y + (1/3)h꜀ₒ + (2/3)r] = (22/7) × 7² × [6 + 19/3 + 14/3] = 154 × [6 + 11] = 154 × 17.

**∴ The correct answer is 2618 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Radius (r) = 7 cm, Cylinder height (h₁) = 6 cm, Total height = 32 cm.

**Formula Used:** Volume of **Cylinder** = πr²h | Volume of **Cone** = (1/3)πr²h | Volume of **Hemisphere** = (2/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c8f70d71ef0da45eaa16b44436f9c1be80f06b25f32f03ba94118b441326053.png] 

⇒ Height of Cone (h₂) = 32 − (Height of Cylinder + Radius of Hemisphere) = 32 − (6 + 7) = 19 cm.

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 6 = 154 × 6 = 924 cm³.

⇒ Volume of Cone = (1/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 19 = (1/3) × 154 × 19 = 2926/3 = 975.33 cm³.

⇒ Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 7 = (2/3) × 154 × 7 = 2156/3 = 718.67 cm³.

⇒ Total Volume = 924 + (2926 + 2156)/3 = 924 + 5082/3 = 924 + 1694 = 2618 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 2618 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of the Structure

TSA = CSA of Cone (πrl) + CSA of Cylinder (2πrh) + CSA of Hemisphere (2πr²), where slant height l = √(r² + h꜀ₒₙₑ²).

Volume Calculation Tip

When components share a **common radius**, factor out πr² or (1/3)πr² to simplify calculations and reduce steps.</p
